key_insight: Controlling the octahedral layer count n produces highly phase-pure 2D perovskite microcrystals, enabling tunable band edges and narrow UV-blue emission.
engineering_relevance: Mixing phase-pure powders offers a route to tailor spectral absorption and photocurrent response for optoelectronic devices, though solar-cell performance is not demonstrated.
method: Synthesize 2D lead bromide perovskite powders using cesium and butylammonium A-cations.
Verify structure and composition using X-ray diffraction and energy-dispersive spectroscopy.
Mix selected n-phase powders and press pellets for spectral and dynamic photocurrent measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports sharp absorption onsets, single narrow emission peaks, and pellet photocurrent responses that depend strongly on powder composition.
watch_item: Translation from pressed pellets to efficient, stable solar cells remains unverified in the abstract.
paper_title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering
